counterevidence: Scores are hand-coded from quoted text; vendors announce selectively and the labs rarely confirm; lab compute commitments are on the circular ledger and excluded here, so the bell reads data and environments, not compute.
definition: Sum over training-input vendors of each vendor's best procurement score in the trailing four quarters, at quarter ends. Rubric: 1 a lab named as customer; 2 revenue or growth attributed to lab demand; 3 a disclosed lab contract or commitment of at least $100M. Derived metric lab_procurement_signal_4q.

direction_rule.rationale: Four quarters; a one-point move is one vendor's single disclosure. Rising = the labs buying more from the training-input layer.

name: Labs buying from the training-input layer (enter bell)

status_events.author: claude
status_events.reason: First reading, quarter to 30 Jun 2026: one training-input vendor scored (Mercor, 2 on the rubric: growth attributed to AI labs buying expert data). The direction rule needs five quarterly readings; not yet measurable until then. Initial seed.

timing_rationale: Leading: labs buy data and environments for models released months later, so purchases precede capability and revenue.
tracker_interpretation: One scored vendor so far (Mercor, revenue attributed to lab demand in June 2026); the sum is a floor until more vendors have a quotable source.
why_it_matters: P1's enter bell: when the labs start buying from the layer below them, that layer's economics turn; read with the exit bell, when they buy the vendors outright.
